usage:
Here is how we can work together.

1. Create a project: tell me a project name and any settings that matter to you — for example the anonymization style (strict or clinical), the imaging modalities to accept, or the language. I will prepare the complete configuration by combining your choices with the standard defaults, then show it to you. Nothing is created yet. You can ask me to change anything and I will show you a revised version; the project is only created when you tell me to go ahead exactly as shown.

2. Change settings later: once a project exists, you can ask me to show its current settings, or simply tell me what to change — for example the modalities, network timeouts, or anonymization style. The project name, storage location, site ID, UID root, and the language chosen when the project was created cannot be changed afterwards.

3. Add DICOM data: with a project open, give me the full path of a DICOM file or a folder of DICOM files and I will import it. Or, if your images are on a hospital PACS, tell me whether it uses DIMSE or DICOMweb and give me its connection details; if you are not sure which it uses, just ask and we will work it out before connecting.

4. Review and process the data: ask me what studies and series are in the project, ask to see a preview image of a series, or ask me to remove burnt-in text from images or tidy up study and series descriptions.

You do not need to know any setting in advance — name the project, mention only what matters to you, and I will handle the rest and check with you before creating anything.
example_requests: Create a new project named DemoCXR. Use defaults for everything else.
Create a clinical project named ClinicalDemo using CT and MR.
Add US and show me the revised configuration.
Yes, create it exactly as shown.
Show me the project defaults and ranges.
Change the modalities to CT, MR and US.
Import the DICOM file at this absolute path: /Users/me/studies/chest.dcm
List what studies and series are in the project.
configuration_confirmation: Call create_project with confirm=false and only the settings the clinician supplied. The server returns the complete ProjectModel configuration (supplied values combined with defaults) and a revision. Present it, then stop. Change the pending configuration with another confirm=false call, or create it only after the clinician explicitly confirms that revision with confirm=true.
anonymization_policy: Strict (default): image-focused anonymization script. Clinical: TCIA-style de-identification that keeps more report/clinical free-text tags and enables SR/PDF modalities. Switching policy on an existing project replaces the project anonymizer script with the packaged policy script (custom script edits are lost).
modalities: Which DICOM modalities this project accepts on ingest. Keep factory defaults unless the clinician needs others. Storage classes are derived from modalities — do not invent a separate storage-class tool.
transfer_syntaxes: Encodings accepted for receive/import. Keep factory defaults unless the clinician specifies transfer-syntax UIDs from the allowed set.
local_scp: This workstation's DICOM receive address (ip, port, AE title). Required when a PACS will C-MOVE studies into this project (DIMSE). Mirrored to the local SCU.
network_timeouts: How long to wait for slow archives (tcp_connection, acse, dimse, network). Keep defaults unless the clinician reports timeouts.
identity_locked: project_name, storage_dir, site_id, uid_root, and language_code are fixed after create; language_code is chosen once at project creation, like the desktop welcome-screen language selector. Use update_project_settings only for modalities, transfer_syntaxes, scp, network_timeouts, and anonymization_policy.
